title: Stellarator coil manufacturing precision
bottleneck: Stellarators confine plasma with intricately shaped 3D magnetic coils that must be built to millimeter precision over tens of meters. Any deviation creates magnetic field errors that degrade confinement. Wendelstein 7-X demonstrated the physics, but its coils took over a decade to build at enormous cost. High-temperature superconductors could shrink stellarators, yet winding brittle REBCO tape into complex 3D shapes without degrading it is unsolved.
why_it_blocks: Stellarators avoid tokamaks' disruption and current-drive problems, but only if their coils can be manufactured affordably and precisely. Otherwise they remain one-off physics experiments rather than power-plant templates.
current_state: W7-X proved steady-state stellarator confinement. Startups are pursuing HTS stellarators with simplified coil designs, but precision HTS 3D coil manufacturing is still developmental.
